pieces.title: He wrote chemistry as an exact science, and went to the guillotine: Lavoisier
pieces.hook: First turn the problem into something you can weigh: Lavoisier did not shout phlogiston theory down; he let the numbers on the balance speak for him.
pieces.takeaway: First turn the problem into something you can weigh: Lavoisier did not shout phlogiston theory down; he let the numbers on the balance speak for him.

parts: Antoine-Laurent de Lavoisier (1743–1794) was a French chemist. He rewrote combustion from a mysterious story of “phlogiston” into a process of combination with oxygen that could be weighed, and he also helped design the metric system.
On 8 May 1794 he was sent to the guillotine in Paris, at the age of 50.

【From tax farmer to chemist】He was born on 26 August 1743 into a legal family in Paris, and he himself trained in law. In 1768 he became a member of the tax-farming company; the post made him rich, and it later gave his judges a hold over him.
In 1771 he married thirteen-year-old Marie-Anne. His wife later translated English papers for him and drew experimental plates; she was an indispensable collaborator in the laboratory.

paras.lead: Combustion was not “the release of phlogiston”
parts: European chemistry was still ruled by phlogiston theory: things burned because they gave off phlogiston. Lavoisier used sealed vessels and a precise balance to show that metals got heavier after calcination because they combined with part of the air. He identified and named oxygen, explained what respiration, combustion and calcination had in common, and stated conservation of mass: in a closed change, the total quantity of matter is neither created nor destroyed; it only changes form.

In 1789 the Elementary Treatise on Chemistry was published, the elements were listed anew, and old names and theories were systematically replaced. Chemistry thereafter looked more like a science that spoke in weights.

He was not only a writer of books. He helped improve the production of gunpowder, paid attention to lighting and water in Paris, and played an important role on the Academy of Sciences’ weights and measures committee. He saw a unified system of measures as just as necessary as a unified chemical language: without a common ruler and a common scale, precise experiments and the governing of a country would each talk past the other.

paras.lead: An old identity in the Revolution
parts: After the French Revolution broke out, both the Academy of Sciences and the tax-farming system came under attack. In 1793 members of the tax-farming company were arrested. Lavoisier had worked for the new regime, including on metric reform, but that did not get him out from under the identity of “a tax farmer of the old regime.”

On 8 May 1794 he and a group of former tax farmers were convicted by the Revolutionary Tribunal and executed. A remark later circulated under Lagrange’s name: it takes only a moment to cut off this head, and a hundred years will not be enough to grow another like it. Whether those were his exact words has since been debated, but the feeling they record is real: many people saw the execution as both a political settling of accounts and a loss to science.

Phlogiston theory left the mainstream; elements, compounds, conservation of mass and clear nomenclature became the chassis of chemistry thereafter. After his death, his wife Marie-Anne continued to organize and publish the records, so that his work did not end with the guillotine.

critical.label: Another angle
items: Lavoisier｜View: Chemistry must be done in a unified language and with repeatable weighing.；Interest: To build a new system, and also to keep the conditions for his own research.；Worry: That the theory would not be accepted, and that his political identity would drag down the work.；Basis: The experiments on oxygen and conservation of mass; the Elementary Treatise on Chemistry.

Supporters of phlogiston theory｜View: The old theory could still explain many phenomena; there was no need to tear it down lightly.；Interest: To keep the academic framework they already had.；Worry: That their system of explanation would lose authority.；Basis: For most of the eighteenth century, phlogiston theory remained the mainstream.

Marie-Anne｜View: Experiments need records, translation and images.；Interest: To have the work transmitted accurately.；Worry: That manuscripts and instruments would be scattered in the upheaval.；Basis: She translated, drew the plates, and after her husband’s death organized and published them.

The revolutionary authorities｜View: Tax farmers stood for the exploitation of the people and had to be called to account.；Interest: Fiscal and political legitimacy.；Worry: That the old group would use scientific prestige to escape judgment.；Basis: Members of the tax-farming company were tried as a group; execution was not waived because of scientific contributions.

The scientific community later on｜View: Politics can put a person to death, but it is much harder to erase a method.；Interest: To preserve a tradition of knowledge that can be tested.；Worry: Of turning the scientist into a saint, or of washing his tax-farmer identity completely away.；Basis: Conservation of mass and the table of elements were generally adopted by later chemistry.

critical.label: Checks and trade-offs
items: Income from tax farming paid for the laboratory, and it also became the heaviest charge in the courtroom.
He wanted to unify the language of chemistry, while working inside a revolution that was breaking the old measures.
Scientific reputation did not convert into a pardon, which shows that the standard of judgment at the time was not scholarly achievement.

critical.label: Where it gets stuck
items: Modern chemistry remembers his balance; history remembers his death sentence. The two memories sit in the same person, and to this day they cannot stand in for each other.

critical.label: Where the evidence is thin
items: Whether that famous remark of Lagrange’s was his exact wording is still disputed in later citations.
His precise role on the weights and measures committee is emphasized to different degrees in different biographies.
The Revolutionary Tribunal’s files on individual guilt carry the colour of a political trial of that time, and should not be treated as the conclusion of a careful financial audit.

pieces.title: Making a metre the same length everywhere: two centuries of the metric system
pieces.short: Two centuries of the metric system
pieces.hook: In the same sale, one place used one “foot” and another used a different “foot”; tax, army rations and experimental data would all fail to line up.

parts: In the same sale, one place used one “foot” and another used a different “foot”; tax, army rations and experimental data would all fail to line up. At the end of the eighteenth century France decided to do one thing: stop relying on the length of some king’s foot or on the scales of some particular town, and, by nature and by agreement, give a set of measures everyone could share.

From 1790 France began to discuss unified measures. In 1791 the Academy of Sciences argued that the “metre” should be defined as one ten-millionth of a quarter of the Earth’s meridian, and sent Delambre, Méchain and others to measure the meridian arc from Dunkirk to Barcelona.

The survey was carried out in the turmoil of the Revolution and took many years. In 1795 France formally adopted the metric system by law: length in metres, mass in kilograms, and a decimal scale of units. In 1799 the platinum metre prototype and kilogram prototype were made, as physical standards.

paras.lead: First in France, then toward a convention
parts: The new ruler was not loved by everyone at once. Merchants and craftsmen used to the old units changed slowly, and shifts of regime also made the rollout start and stop. But trade and science needed a common language.

On 20 May 1875, 17 countries signed the Metre Convention in Paris and established the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, turning the keeping and comparison of the metre and the kilogram into an international public affair. Thereafter the metric system went from a French reform to the legal foundation of many countries.

In 1960 the International System of Units (SI) was formally named, organizing the metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, candela and others into one set. Later the “metre” no longer depended on a metal bar: in 1983 it was defined as the distance light travels in vacuum in a specified time.

In 2019 the kilogram and other base units were also redefined by natural constants, and no longer depended on a prototype in a vault. The rulers are still in use; the definition has left that platinum bar behind.

paras.lead: How China switched to legal units
parts: Traditional Chinese measures and the metric system coexisted for a long time. In 1984 the State Council issued an order to implement legal units of measurement uniformly, on the basis of the International System of Units, requiring the transition to be completed by the end of 1990, and from 1991, except in a few special fields, non-legal units would no longer be used.

Today textbooks, medicine labels, engineering drawings and trade contracts already default to the metre, the kilogram and the litre. In the marketplace you can still hear the “jin,” but that is a habit of daily life, no longer the main language of national measurement.

Units are still getting finer】Most countries and scientific publications already use SI. A few places, including the United States, still keep imperial units in everyday life, while using the metric system in science, the military and some industries, a dual track. The precision demanded by chips, satellites and medicines has long been beyond what that eighteenth-century metre prototype could give directly, but the principle has not changed: only after a common unit is agreed can a measurement be repeated by someone else.

critical.label: Another angle
items: Scientists and metrology institutes｜View: Units must be reproducible and cannot rest on local habit.；Interest: Experiments can be checked, and standards can be passed on.；Worry: That a prototype would be damaged, or that a definition would not be stable enough.；Basis: The move from metal prototypes to definitions by constants.

Governments and tax and military-supply departments｜View: Only unified measures can tax fairly and allocate supplies fairly.；Interest: The efficiency of government and the authority of the system.；Worry: That reform would provoke resistance.；Basis: France enacted the system during the Revolution; China completed the transition to legal units in about a decade.

Merchants and craftsmen｜View: Changing the ruler means changing every old account and every mould.；Interest: Fewer disputes in trade across regions.；Worry: Errors and costs in the transition period.；Basis: In every country the metric system went through a stage of coexistence with old units.

Societies that have not fully switched to the metric system｜View: Everyday habit is also a kind of cost.；Interest: To keep the rulers, road signs and tools they already have.；Worry: That a dual track will cause confusion or even accidents.；Basis: Daily life in the United States still commonly uses imperial units, while science mostly uses SI.

Precision manufacturing and high-technology industry｜View: Error has to be placed inside a shared scale that is extremely small.；Interest: Global supply chains can fit together.；Worry: That parts will not match if standards are not the same.；Basis: Modern industry and laboratories generally use SI as their working language.

critical.label: Checks and trade-offs
items: Defining the “metre” by the Earth’s meridian sounds natural, but the survey itself was slow, laborious and full of error, and only later was the definition changed to the speed of light.
The state wants uniformity, people want convenience, so legal units and spoken habits have long existed side by side.
An international convention lets standards be shared, and also requires countries to hand part of the power of definition to a common system of measurement.

critical.label: Where it gets stuck
items: Units can be rewritten with great precision, but if the classroom, the workshop and the marketplace each use a different set, the precision stays only on paper.

critical.label: Where the evidence is thin
items: Some details of error in the meridian survey at the end of the eighteenth century belong to specialist histories of metrology; this piece takes only the main line of institutional reform.
“Complete the transition by the end of 1990” was a policy target; the actual pace of conversion was not perfectly even from place to place.
Cases of accidents caused by mixed-up units are often cited; the specific causes need to be checked case by case, and this piece does not use them as statistics.

pieces.title: This quarter’s sales were down a fifth, but the share price rose 8%: Take-Two before GTA 6 launched
pieces.hook: For a company about to launch a blockbuster, you have to look at the quarter just ended, the next quarter’s guidance and the still-unchecked pre-orders together, rather…
pieces.takeaway: For a company about to launch a blockbuster, you have to look at the quarter just ended, the next quarter’s guidance and the still-unchecked pre-orders together, rather than only at the numbers already booked.
pieces.event: 2026-11-09 released fiscal 2027 second-quarter results; 11-10 closed up 8.31% in New York; GTA VI set for release on 11-19

parts: On 9 November, the New York game publisher Take-Two Interactive released its results for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (ended 30 September): net bookings of $1.60 billion, 18% less than $1.96 billion a year earlier; under US GAAP, net revenue of $1.50 billion and a net loss of $54 million, or $0.29 a share. The loss was smaller than the $133.9 million, or $0.73 a share, a year earlier.
The next day it closed at $224.64 on the New York Stock Exchange, up 8.31%.

Take-Two is the home of Grand Theft Auto (GTA), Red Dead Redemption and NBA 2K, with studios including Rockstar, 2K and Zynga. In the games industry, people more often watch “net bookings”: the digital and physical products actually sold in the period, not when revenue is recognized in the accounts.
The company treats this as the main ruler for watching the business.

paras.lead: This quarter still leaned on old titles
parts: Of the $1.60 billion, 81% came from “recurrent consumer spending”: virtual currency, additional content and advertising in the games, 9% less than a year earlier. The largest contributors the company listed were titles already on the market, including NBA 2K, the GTA series, Toon Blast and Match Factory!.
In other words, the new blockbuster has not yet hit the books, and the old catalogue has already shrunk a notch on its own.

【GTA 6 lifted the next quarter】In the same earnings report, the company reiterated that Grand Theft Auto VI will go on sale on 19 November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Chairman and chief executive Strauss Zelnick said the launch was “ten days away,” that pre-orders “continue to be at unprecedented levels,” and that he expected this to be a “historic year” for the company.

The company maintained its outlook for fiscal 2027 net bookings of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion, and for the third quarter ending 31 December gave net-bookings guidance of $3.35 billion to $3.50 billion—about twice the second quarter. Third-quarter net-income guidance was $250 million to $276 million, or $1.30 to $1.44 a share.

paras.lead: The pre-order figures were not published separately
parts: “Unprecedented” is the company’s own wording. This earnings report did not give a specific number of pre-orders or their value, and did not break GTA VI out separately from the third-quarter guidance. What investors saw was a whole quarter of raised outlook, and the share-price reaction on 10 November, when volume was about 8.19 million shares, 3.1 times the average daily volume of the previous three months (compiled by Nexqual from trading data).

paras.lead: Who benefits, who is under pressure
parts: The first to benefit were people who already held the shares or bought them that day: they rose 8.31% in a day, and the company’s market value was then about $42 billion. Sony and Microsoft, as the launch console platforms, will also be tied to this blockbuster. Under pressure are players still buying in-game items in old titles: recurrent consumer spending has already fallen; and people waiting for the PC version, whose release date has not been announced.
The studio itself has to finish the launch preparations in ten days; any delay would run straight into this third-quarter guidance just given.

The facts are: second-quarter net bookings fell 18%, and the company was still loss-making under US GAAP; the full-year net-bookings outlook was left unchanged, and third-quarter guidance was markedly higher than the second quarter; the next day the share price rose 8.31%. The inference is: the rise came from the market pricing in GTA VI’s first-week sales in advance—which matches the company’s remarks about pre-orders, but the scale of pre-orders itself has not been independently disclosed, and one cannot split out of a single day’s share price “how much came from the game and how much from market mood.”

When you look at a company about to launch a blockbuster, looking only at the quarter just ended will often give you a conclusion that runs the other way from the share price. It is more worth lining up three things: whether the old catalogue is still selling, how high the next quarter has been lifted, and whether the company has turned “pre-orders are strong” into numbers that can be checked.

critical.label: Another angle
items: Company management｜View: GTA VI will bring a historic year, pre-orders have already reached unprecedented levels, and the full-year target can be maintained.；Interest: A smooth launch, delivering the full-year net bookings, and expanding products and acquisitions thereafter.；Worry: That a launch delay or first-week sales below internal expectations would run straight into the third-quarter guidance just given.；Basis: The 11-9 earnings report and Zelnick’s remarks; full-year net-bookings outlook of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion, and third-quarter guidance of $3.35 billion to $3.50 billion.

Shareholders and short-term investors｜View: The market has already written the next quarter’s blockbuster into the share price.；Interest: The valuation and the day’s gain.；Worry: That the scale of pre-orders cannot be checked, and that if the guidance is not met the gain may be given back.；Basis: On 11-10 it closed at $224.64, up 8.31%, on volume of about 8.19 million shares, 3.1 times the three-month average daily volume (Nexqual).

Existing players and recurrent consumer spending｜View: What is hitting the books right now is still old titles and in-game purchases.；Interest: Whether the game experience and the willingness to pay will continue.；Worry: Whether the shrinking catalogue means the gap before the blockbuster arrives is more obvious.；Basis: Recurrent consumer spending was 81% of net bookings, down 9% year on year; the largest contributors were still NBA 2K, the GTA series and a group of mobile games (company earnings report).

Console platforms (Sony, Microsoft)｜View: The launch window ties this blockbuster to their respective machines.；Interest: Console sales and a share of the platform store.；Worry: That the absence of a PC version may push some players later, or toward a rival.；Basis: The company confirmed a 19 November release only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S; the earnings report did not announce a PC date.

Securities analysts｜View: Some remain bullish, and some have nudged their price targets.；Interest: Investment ratings and clients’ positions.；Worry: Whether the third quarter can reach the top of the guidance range, and whether profits will be sustainable after the blockbuster.；Basis: Nexqual recorded: on 11-10 UBS cut its target from $300 to $295 and kept a Buy; BTIG reiterated Buy, with a target of $262.

critical.label: Checks and trade-offs
items: The second quarter already sold a fifth less, yet third-quarter guidance is about doubled: between the two sits a day that has not yet arrived.

The company is backing the outlook with “unprecedented pre-orders,” but has not published pre-order numbers that can be checked, so shareholders can only work backwards from the share price and next quarter’s guidance.
Recurrent consumer spending has already fallen, which shows that before the blockbuster hits the books, the old catalogue cannot fully hold up the scale.

critical.label: Where it gets stuck
items: The share price has already added a premium for the 19 November launch; and the scale of pre-orders, first-week actual sales and the PC timetable are all still without publicly checkable figures.

critical.label: Where the evidence is thin
items: “Unprecedented pre-orders” came with no specific number of copies or amount of money, and cannot be compared directly with earlier titles.
Of a one-day rise of 8.31%, how much came from the game itself and how much from the market mood of the moment cannot be split out.
The third-quarter guidance is a range, and does not guarantee that the actual result will land at the top or the bottom.

pieces.title: He won more than 60 percent, but fewer than a third of people voted: Cabo Verde elects a president
pieces.hook: The West African island nation of Cabo Verde held a presidential election on 15 November.
pieces.event: 2026-11-15 presidential election day; at the time of writing official provisional results had counted 96.5% of polling stations, and a final winner had not yet been declared

parts: The West African island nation of Cabo Verde held a presidential election on 15 November. According to the official provisional results site eleicoes.cv, at the time of writing 1,251 of 1,296 polling stations (96.5%) had been counted: the incumbent president, José Maria Neves, had 79,988 votes, or 63.8%; the main challenger, former justice minister Joana Gomes Rosa Amado, had 39,649 votes, or 31.6%.

The official site marked him as “likely to win in the first round.” At the same time, of the 404,127 registered voters on the counted rolls, only 129,192 people voted, a turnout of 32%, with 274,935 abstentions, or 68%.

paras.lead: How this country elects a president
parts: Cabo Verde became independent from Portugal in 1975, and is one of the few countries in West Africa with long-running multiparty alternation, regarded by observers as politically stable. It has a mix of parliamentary and presidential systems: the president has a veto and a mediating role, and day-to-day administration is the prime minister’s. In May this year, the African Party for the Independence of Cabo Verde (PAICV), to which Neves belongs, won 37 of 72 seats, and he appointed the mayor of Praia, Francisco Carvalho, as prime minister.
A president must win more than 50% of valid votes to be elected in the first round; otherwise the top two will go to a runoff on 29 November.

Among the valid votes already counted, Neves had about twice as many votes as Rosa, leading by about 40,000 votes, or 32.2 percentage points. The other four candidates without the backing of the two main parties—Gilson Alves, Antero Tavares, Casimiro Pina and Luisito Sousa—each had less than 1.5% of the vote.

Lusa, citing the official line, said that in 2021 Neves also won in the first round, but then with only 51.8%, against 42.4% for Carlos Veiga, a founder of the Movement for Democracy. If the remaining ballot boxes after 96.5% do not produce a large reversal, he will close off the possibility of a “must-have runoff,” and continue the record that “every elected president who has run for re-election has succeeded.”
These are still provisional figures; a final winner must wait for the official declaration.

What stings more is not who won, but who did not come. Turnout on the counted rolls was only 32%, with 68% abstaining. Lusa reported that the abstention rate in the 2021 presidential election was 52%.

In other words, in five years the number of people who did not vote has grown by another large slice. Lusa also wrote: of about 419,400 registered voters nationwide, about 76,400 were overseas citizens, or 18%. Al Jazeera and the Associated Press reported on polling day that there are about 500,000 people on the islands, and more Cabo Verdeans living abroad than on the islands, mainly in Portugal and the United States; the focus of the election debate was precisely how to slow the continuing outflow of young people.
The official site has not yet published turnout for overseas ballot boxes separately, so one still cannot simply write “abstention” as “the diaspora did not come back to vote.”

Rosa is the first woman to run for president since independence in 1975, backed by the opposition Movement for Democracy (MpD). The party had governed for ten years before the May parliamentary election, and she herself had been minister of justice. Al Jazeera quoted her argument: young people should “build their future at home, and keep the young from continuing to leave.”

Neves, for his part, promised that if re-elected he would organize a youth summit to discuss migration. At the time of writing she had 31.6% of the valid vote, more than 30 percentage points behind the leader, and on the current provisional results a runoff may not be held.

paras.lead: Some have written abstention as a “disaster”
parts: Gilson Alves, the candidate in third place, told the national radio that an abstention rate this high was a “disaster” for Cabo Verde’s democracy, that it would weaken the political legitimacy of the president-elect, and that he would not congratulate the future winner. He also planned to complain to the National Electoral Commission about the attorney general’s conduct during the campaign.

This is a candidate’s position, not a conclusion of the electoral authorities. About 150 observers from six international organizations were present for the vote; at the time of writing, no final assessment from the observer missions had been seen.

paras.lead: A narrative frame to watch for
parts: One account would write 63.8% as a “landslide mandate”; another would write 68% abstention as “the election has no legitimacy.” The provisional results contain both facts at once: among those who already voted, Neves was clearly over half; among the registered voters already counted, only about one person in three voted.

How strong the mandate is depends on whether you put the denominator on “valid votes” or on “all registered voters.” Likewise, attributing low turnout directly to the diaspora or to young people still lacks breakdowns of the data. The final count and official declaration are not yet complete, and this piece does not let provisional figures stand in for an official announcement of the winner.

critical.label: Another angle
items: Neves and the ruling PAICV｜View: Seek to complete a second term in the first round, and treat the outflow of young people as a question that has to be answered.；Interest: A second presidential term, and coordination with the parliamentary majority and the appointment of the prime minister.；Worry: That too low a turnout will be used by opponents to question the mandate; remaining ballot boxes and the official declaration are still unfinished.；Basis: In the provisional count he had 63.8%, leading by 32.2 percentage points (eleicoes.cv); Al Jazeera quoted his promise to organize a youth summit.

Rosa and the opposition MpD｜View: Want young people to stay and build at home, and to challenge the incumbent president.；Interest: After the party lost parliamentary control in May, it still hopes to take the presidency.；Worry: That the gap with the leader is too large, and it may not be possible to push the election into a 29 November runoff.；Basis: She is the first woman presidential candidate since independence, with a provisional 31.6%; her arguments were reported by Al Jazeera / AP on polling day.

Gilson Alves and the smaller candidates｜View: High abstention damages the political legitimacy of the person elected.；Interest: To keep a political voice by raising the abstention issue, and to question the campaign process.；Worry: Their own vote shares are very low, and their arguments may not change the count.；Basis: Alves had a provisional 1.4%; he told national radio that abstention was a “disaster,” said he would not congratulate the winner, and planned to complain to the electoral commission about the attorney general (reported by Balai).

The diaspora and registered voters｜View: Migration and a path for young people are among the central issues of this election.；Interest: Representation of home, and convenience of life abroad.；Worry: Being registered does not mean voting, and those not registered are even less on the roll.；Basis: Lusa: of about 419,400 registered voters nationwide, about 76,400 were overseas citizens, or 18%; Al Jazeera said more people live abroad than the about 500,000 residents on the islands. Overseas turnout has not yet been published separately on the official site.

Electoral authorities and observers｜View: Publish provisional results first, then complete the official count and declaration.；Interest: A procedure that can be checked, and a result that can be accepted.；Worry: Writing provisional figures as a final winner before the count is finished.；Basis: eleicoes.cv marks the results as provisional and says “likely to win in the first round”; Lusa said about 150 observers came from six international organizations. At the time of writing, no final assessment from the observer missions had been published.

critical.label: Checks and trade-offs
items: Among those who already voted, Neves was clearly over half; among registered voters, abstention was the majority. The two sides that support and that question the “mandate” are using the same set of provisional figures, but different denominators.

During the campaign everyone was talking about the outflow of young people, yet turnout is lower than five years ago. Raising an issue does not automatically become a reason for people to go and vote.
Rosa took second place as the first woman candidate, but the gap with the leader is already more than 30 percentage points, and the window for a runoff is narrowing.

critical.label: Where it gets stuck
items: The provisional results already point to a first-round winner, but an official election has not yet been declared; low turnout has been written by some candidates as a crisis of legitimacy, but breakdowns of the data (age, diaspora, the islands at home) have not been published, so the reasons still cannot be fixed.

critical.label: Where the evidence is thin
items: This piece uses provisional results from 96.5% of ballot boxes; the remaining 3.5% may still nudge the percentages, and cannot take the place of a final official announcement.
The 2021 abstention rate of 52% is cited from Lusa; this piece has not seen the matching official historical tables in the original.
Separate turnout figures for overseas and young voters, and the specific reasons for abstention, had no citable breakdowns or authoritative polls at the time of writing.
